reader.requirement: At --std 85 each SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS integer-1 must name an ordinal position that exists in the native character set (implementor-defined; this implementation's native set is 65,536 UTF-16 code units, ordinals 1..65536) or, under IN alphabet-name-2, in that alphabet's character set (STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 128, NATIVE the native set, an implementor-name such as EBCDIC its own count, a literal-phrase alphabet its distinct positions after ALSO merging); an ordinal outside the set (0, one past the end) must be refused and one inside must bind the character at that position.

edition-consulted.switches: the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL phrase is a 2002 introduction (COBOL0900 at 85)

reader.edition-search: SwitchBindSymbolic, CodedCharacterSetOf, CodedCharacterSet.OrdinalCount/CharAt and CollatingTable.Repertoire read no edition (grep 'Edition\.|DialectLevel' in SpecialNamesBinder.Classes.cs finds only Edition.At/Edition.Error); the native set and the range check are the same code at every --std. The only edition consultation on the clause's path is the FOR-phrase gate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for the ordinal range); the FOR phrase is refused at 85 only
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1557 covers an ordinal far beyond the native set and pb110 the SR9 pairing; no witness covers ordinal 0, the native upper bound, or any IN alphabet (STANDARD-1/2, NATIVE, implementor-name, literal phrase with THRU/ALSO)

reader.notes: SwitchBindSymbolic resolves each ordinal through CodedCharacterSet.CharAt (IN) or the native repertoire, refusing a missing position with COBOL1670; every bound, alphabet kind and ALSO merge probed behaves as the 1985 text requires. The message for a literal-phrase alphabet with ALSO says '65536 characters' although the set has 65535 positions (cosmetic; the refusal is right). Diagnostics cite §2023 at --std 85.
reader.at-2023: c4-ord65537 and c4-std1-129 refused identically at --std 2023

refuter.evidence: Attack on the scope of the 1985 IN phrase: in the corrected 1985 format (Amendment 1 C124) one SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause is {{symbolic-character-1}... IS|ARE {integer-1}...}... [IN alphabet-name-2], so IN governs EVERY pair of the clause, not only the last. Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-049/src/r4-*.cob): 'S1 IS 129 S2 IS 5 IN A-STD1' -> COBOL1670 'S1 IS 129 ... does not exist in ... STANDARD-1, 128 characters' (IN reaches the first group); 'S1 S2 ARE 129 66 IN A-STD1' -> same; 'S1 IS 194 S2 IS 195 IN A-EBC' -> EXIT 0 [A][B] (both bound through EBCDIC, not native: native 194 would be U+00C1); 'S1 S2 ARE 66 65537' -> COBOL1670 on S2 (every integer checked, not only the first); two clauses, IN on the first only ('S1 IS 194 IN A-EBC SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS S2 IS 194') -> [A][Á] (IN does not leak into the next clause); implementor-name ASCII: 129 -> COBOL1670 (128 characters), 128 -> EXIT 0. The native set's size (65536 UTF-16 positions) is implementor-defined and applied consistently. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR10  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR10; OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4d  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4d.
